Additional District Judge & Mact, Hassan, Dismissing
The Claim Petition For Compensation.

This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:

Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice N S Sanjay Gowda
 Oral Judgment
1. An accident occurred on 01.07.2016 between the claimant and the motorcycle, which resulted in lodging of a claim petition claiming compensation for the injuries suffered by the claimant.
2. The Tribunal has dismissed the claim petition on two grounds.

Firstly, the Consent Form given for the surgery indicated that the wife had affixed the signature signifying her consent, but the medical records indicated that the claimant was brought to NC: 2024:KHC:50720 the hospital by one Manju and, therefore, this discrepancy had created a doubt in the mind of the Tribunal regarding the occurrence of the accident.
Secondly, there was a delay of one day in lodging the FIR which confirmed the doubt.

3. At the outset, it is to be stated that once a victim of a motor vehicle accident approaches a hospital and complains of injuries due to a road traffic accident, it becomes incumbent on the hospital to inform the authorities and the delay, if any, in lodging the FIR would really be of no significance.
In the instant case, the evidence on record clearly indicates that the claimant was brought to the hospital and the hospital authorities did inform the Alur Police Station on 02.07.2016.

4. In my view, since the claimant had gone to the hospital and informed the authorities that he had suffered injuries as a result of motor vehicle accident, the delay, if any, in lodging the FIR would NC:
2024:KHC:50720 be really of no consequence.
Consequently, the reasoning of the Tribunal cannot be accepted and the same is set aside.

2 5.

Though, in the normal cases, the matter would have been remanded to the Tribunal for re-consideration for assessing the compensation, having regard to the fact that the accident is of the year 2016, it would be appropriate to assess the compensation in this appeal itself.
6. The evidence on record indicates that the claimant had suffered a fracture of tibia and fibula.
The claimant was aged about 36 years and was working as a barber.
7. In my view, having regard to the nature of the avocation and the injuries suffered, it would be appropriate to treat the disability at 10% to the whole body.

Since there is no proof of actual income,
as determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services NC: 2024:KHC:50720 Authority the notional income as Rs.9,500/- for the accident of the year 2016, it would be appropriate to determine the notional income of the claimant at Rs.9,500/-.

sentences.text: 8. Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,71,000/- (Rs.9,500/- X 12 X '15'X 10%) towards 'loss of future earnings'.
9. The claimant had produced medical evidence to indicate that he has spent Rs.35,490/- towards 'medical expenses'.
Since it is based on documentary evidence, the same will have to be granted.

10. The claimant is also entitled to a sum of Rs.50,000/-
towards 'pain and sufferings' and Rs.50,000/- 'loss of amenities'.
11.

Having regard to the length of hospitalization, it would be appropriate to award Rs.10,000/-
towards 'conveyance, food, nutrition and attendant charges'.

Since the claimant had suffered fracture of tibia and fibula, it would be appropriate to treat the laid-up period as three months and consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.28,500/- (Rs.9,500/- X 3 months) towards 'loss of earnings during laid up period'.

13. Consequently, the claimant is entitled to the following sums as compensation:
As awarded Sl. by this Compensation under No. Court different Heads (Rs.)
1. Pain and sufferings 50,000/-
2. Loss of future earnings 1,71,000/-
3. Medical expenses 35,490/-
Loss of income during the laid 28,500/-

3 4.
up period Conveyance, nourishment and 10,000/-
5. nutritious food

6 . Loss of amenities in life 50,000/-
 Total 3,44,990/-
14. Accordingly, the claimant is held entitled for compensation of Rs.3,44,990/- along with interest NC: 2024:KHC:50720 at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation.
15. However, the claimant would not be entitled for interest for the delayed period as per order dated 29.05.2024.
16. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

17. Upon deposit, 40% of the compensation amount shall be invested in a fixed deposit for a period of three in the name of claimant in any Nationalised or Scheduled Bank of the claimant's choice with liberty to withdraw the interest accrued thereon, periodically, on the compensation amount.
After maturity, the Bank shall release the amount in favour of claimant.
The remaining compensation amount NC: 2024:KHC:50720 shall be released in favour of claimant after proper identification.
18. The appeal is, accordingly, allowed in part.
